options.content:
**Cellular Threat Detection** — signals drawn from `docs/DETECTION-SIGNALS.md`, priority-ordered against 3GPP TR 33.809 (rogue-base-station study, all 7 key issues closed "not concluded" - no normative fake-base-station detection exists in 5G). This lab observes from the **core** side (AMF/SMF/UPF/PCF Prometheus metrics), which is a different and more operationally realistic vantage point than the UE-side detectors most published research assumes.

**Centrepiece: Authentication Failures by 5GMM Cause.** `fivegs_amffunction_amf_authfail` carries the literal NAS 5GMM cause number as a label - confirmed live on this lab. **Cause 20 = MAC failure** (the UE rejected the network's challenge - a forged/replayed authentication vector, the signature of a false base station or replay attack). **Cause 21 = Synch failure** (SQN out of range - consistent with a replayed AUTN, i.e. a captured challenge being replayed later). These two causes are shown as **separate series** below so an analyst can tell which failure mode is occurring, not just that failures are occurring.

An analyst should watch for: (1) any non-zero cause-20 rate from a single subscriber/cell, (2) repeated cause-21 (sync failure) bursts, (3) registration or auth request rate spikes without matching success growth, (4) `ran_ue` and `amf_session` diverging (a MITM/relay can hold a RAN-side context open without a matching AMF session, or vice versa), (5) paging requests with no matching paging success.

panels.title: Authentication Failures by Cause (centrepiece)
panels.description: fivegs_amffunction_amf_authfail{cause=...}. cause=20 => MAC failure (forged/replayed challenge). cause=21 => Synch failure (SQN desync, consistent with AUTN replay). Any sustained cause=20 from one subscriber is the strongest single signal this lab can raise for a false base station or an authentication-vector replay attack.

panels.title: Registration Failures by Cause
panels.description: fivegs_amffunction_rm_reginitfail{cause=...}. cause=7 observed on this lab = Illegal UE (e.g. UE attempted registration before its subscriber record existed in UDM/UDR). Non-zero, unexplained cause values here indicate rejected registration attempts and are worth correlating with the auth-failure panel above.

panels.title: Authentication Rejects
panels.description: fivegs_amffunction_amf_authreject - NAS Authentication Reject sent by the network (e.g. ngKSI already in use, cause 22). Track per-subscriber thresholds; a burst suggests repeated failed authentication attempts against one identity.

panels.title: Registration Request Rate (Flood Detection)
panels.description: rate(fivegs_amffunction_rm_reginitreq[1m]) over a sliding window. A sustained rate increase with no matching increase in legitimate subscribers is consistent with a registration flood (DoS against the AMF, or a rogue UE/gNB hammering the core).

panels.title: Registration Success Ratio (Collapse Detection)
panels.description: fivegs_amffunction_rm_reginitsucc / fivegs_amffunction_rm_reginitreq. Should sit near 1.0 on a healthy network. A ratio collapsing toward 0 while request volume stays flat or rises indicates something is actively preventing successful registration - a rogue cell intercepting/jamming signalling, a config fault, or an attack.

panels.title: RAN UE vs AMF Session Divergence (MITM / Relay)
panels.description: ran_ue vs amf_session. These two gauges should track together 1:1 on a healthy network. Sustained divergence (RAN-side context without a matching AMF session, or vice versa) is consistent with a relay/MITM proxy sitting between the RAN and the core, or a NAS/NGAP desync attack.

panels.title: Paging Request vs Success Divergence
panels.description: fivegs_amffunction_mm_paging5greq vs mm_paging5gsucc. Excessive paging requests for one subscriber with no corresponding success (UE never answers) can indicate the UE is out of coverage of the legitimate network - or is camped on a rogue cell that is not forwarding paging, isolating it from the real network.

panels.title: Signals not yet instrumentable from this lab

options.content: Per `docs/DETECTION-SIGNALS.md`, signals #3 (null-scheme SUCI), #5 (cell-identity allowlist violation), #11 (2G cipher-mode A5/0), and #12 (2G identity request pre-ciphering) require decoding NGAP/NAS IEs or GSMTAP capture directly - they are not exposed as Prometheus counters by Open5GS and are out of scope for this Prometheus/Grafana pass. They remain the natural next step (a packet-capture-driven detector) rather than a dashboard panel.
